title: What an Irresistible Offer Looks Like
lede: See a complete roofing offer, why it works and where you use it.
deliverable: You understand the six lines and how the same offer appears in your marketing.
body:
See one complete offer before writing yours.

Jarvis uses the offer creation skill to turn your buyer, problem and solution into six lines. First, see the finished example so you know what you are building.

An offer tells the buyer what you will do for them. Here is a roofing recovery offer written in the same six lines you will use for yours.

The roofer wants more paid jobs. The system follows up quotes they have already sent, so the offer does not depend on buying more ad traffic. The number and guarantee need a large enough pipeline and a delivery plan behind them.

Why this makes it easy to say yes

You are offering the thing the roofer actually wants: more paid jobs. There is a specific target, a clear timeframe and a guarantee that reduces their risk.

They can see how it works: follow up quotes they have already sent. They do not need to spend more on ads to create another batch of enquiries. When the target is realistic for their pipeline and they believe you can deliver it, the offer becomes an easy decision.

Where do you actually use your offer?

Your offer is the promise you repeat throughout your marketing and sales. The wording can change to fit the format, but the result you promise stays the same.

  • Landing page: the headline says what they get; the subheadline explains how.
  • Ads: lead with the result and give them a reason to learn more.
  • Emails and DMs: explain who you help and what you can do for them.
  • VSL: explain the problem, the result and how your service delivers it.
  • Sales calls and proposals: explain what you will do for that business and the terms you agree.

Headline: We’ll get you 5 more roofing jobs in 30 days. Or we work for free.

Subheadline: We build and run an AI follow-up system that turns your unsold roof estimates into paid jobs, without increasing your ad spend.

That is the shape of the roofing example. The number needs a suitable pipeline and a delivery plan behind it.

The headline sells the result. The subheadline explains the mechanism. The VSL explains the service in more depth. Your application finds the right businesses, then the booking page gets them onto a call.
